title: Synergies and Post-Acquisition Performance: Differences versus Similarities in Resource Allocations

rival_explanations: differences in resource allocations (rather than similarities) create unique/private synergy and higher post-acquisition performance
similarities in resource allocations create valuable synergy through economies of scale and scope

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (acquisitions across a number of industries)
context.sample_size: ~1,100 acquired firms matched (per-test N: 441 capital, 396 administrative, 429 debt, 198 R&D intensity)

data_sources.name: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file

dv.name: Post-acquisition performance
dv.source: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file

key_ivs.name: Capital intensity difference
key_ivs.measure: Absolute value of the difference between acquiring and acquired firms in capital intensity, calculated by dividing the dollar amount of capital expenditures by total revenues; base year = year prior to merger
key_ivs.source: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file

key_ivs.name: Administrative intensity difference
key_ivs.measure: Absolute value of the difference between acquiring and acquired firms in administrative (selling, general, and administrative) intensity = SG&A expenditures divided by total revenues; base year = year prior to merger
key_ivs.source: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file

key_ivs.name: Interest (debt) intensity difference
key_ivs.measure: Absolute value of the difference between acquiring and acquired firms in debt (interest expense) intensity = interest expense divided by total revenues; base year = year prior to merger
key_ivs.source: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file

key_ivs.name: R&D intensity difference
key_ivs.measure: Absolute value of the difference between acquiring and acquired firms in R&D intensity = R&D expenditures divided by total revenues; base year = year prior to merger
key_ivs.source: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file

controls.name: Mean Adjusted ROA Before (pre-acquisition industry-adjusted performance; combined income statements of both partners)
controls.source: Standard and Poor's COMPUSTAT research file
